items.root_cause: No rule moved anything: rules_hash a88fe11831a1 equals the one the baseline was accepted against, commodities.json is unchanged since dc4be7174, and drift_vs_engine is 0. The alert is the carried-forward shape the audit names itself: the 2026-09-23 02:02 accept ran while the four dropped names were absent from the corpus, Merge-BaselineCarryForward kept them at the routes they had before dc4be7174's reviewed excludes ('\branch\b' on carrots and cucumbers, the bottled-drink excludes on tea-bags, '\bwisps?\b' on toothbrushes), and when they reappeared in today's captures they routed to nothing exactly as those rules intend. The four new-contested names are genuinely new arrivals (Aldi weekly ad from 2026-09-23, Hy-Vee weekly ad from 2026-09-21, Baker's capture 2026-09-23, Aldi everyday 2026-09-24) that two rules each admit. The one wrong route (Deutsche Küche to chickpeas) is left without a rule change on purpose: the obvious exclude ('\blentil\b' on chickpeas) re-lands the name on brown-lentils via its include '\blentils?\b', where 28 oz at $3.15 is $1.80/lb, BELOW the Walmart brown-lentils crown of $1.92/lb, so the naive fix turns an inert wrong route into a potential wrong CROWN; and a flavour-word exclude ('harvest potato') is a brand-word patch the founding rule refuses. The name is seasonal (German-week ad ending 2026-09-29), holds no cell, and is not an engine candidate.
